instruction: To help with vowel recognition, please make all words that start with vowels (a, e, i, o, u) both italic and blue in color.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires making vowel-starting words both italic AND blue. Verified from word list: 11 words start with vowels (all, am, eat, are, on, at, our, ate, out, into, under). Evaluator uses partial credit: 0.5 for italic formatting, 0.5 for blue color. Uses fuzzy color matching with threshold=20.0.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: 0.5 for italic formatting on all vowel words, 0.5 for blue color on all vowel words

llm_judge_reasons: Critical: Metric only processes text in document.tables, but sight word documents may have words in regular paragraphs. If the document has words outside tables, they will be completely ignored, failing to verify the full instruction.

Significant: Word-level logic error - the metric treats each run.text as a single word and only checks if the first character is a vowel. If multiple words are formatted together in the same run (e.g., 'all am eat'), it would only check 'a' and treat the entire run as one word. Should split run.text into individual words.
The partial credit scoring (0.5 italic + 0.5 color) is semantically correct for the instruction requirements.
The color comparison using CIEDE2000 with threshold=20.0 is appropriate for fuzzy blue matching.
The postconfig correctly saves the file before verification.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Change iteration from 'for table in document.tables' to also process 'for paragraph in document.paragraphs' to cover all document text, not just tables.
Split run.text into individual words (e.g., run.text.split()) and check each word independently instead of treating the entire run as a single word.
Example fix: 'for word in run.text.split(): if word.strip() and word.strip()[0].lower() in "aeiou": ...' to properly handle multiple words in the same formatting run.
